authoredNote: Expectations written from the Svelte 5 rule that an event handler's arrow parameters bind in the TEMPLATE scope (they are not component members), and from the corpus file the defect was measured on — packages/svelte/tests/compiler-errors/samples/store-template-expression-scope/main.svelte, whose handler is `on:click={(store) => { $store = … }}` over a component that declares `const store = writable()`. Line pins read off the post-fix run and checked against the fixture's text. The graph contract is ONE edge per `type|source|target`, so `payload` is published once at its LAST site (42) and `meta.templateReadLines` is where the earlier site (38) is stated; the `[36]` array on `store` is what proves line 42's handler was not silenced by the parameter bound on line 36.
rationale: JOB 2 of the svelte ontology pass. A handler's own arrow parameters were read as component members, which publishes a DANGLING endpoint: nothing in the template scope declares them. Exactly 1 corpus edge in 6,439 files, and it is not a position — the shadow set is widened per EXPRESSION and never per block, so it cannot leak into a sibling, which line 46 pins (`after` is a parameter on line 44 and a real read on line 46). The opposite failure is pinned too: a fix that shadowed the whole handler expression would also silence the `$store` read on line 36, which is the read that actually resolves to a member. And a bare `on:click={save}` has no arrow at all, so it stays BOTH a call target and a read of the member it names.

forbidRelationships.comment: `(evt) => { payload = evt }` — `evt` is the arrow's own parameter. Before this change the analyzer published `uses -> evt`, an endpoint that resolves to nothing.

`({ data }) => { payload = data }` — a DESTRUCTURED parameter binds `data`, so the body read on line 42 names the template-local, not the script's `let data = 3`. A first version of the parameter scan took the first word of the pattern instead of its binding position and published this.
a parameter is not a call target: `(evt) => { payload = evt }` invokes nothing
`{ $store = 1 }` is an assignment, not an invocation
